role: Property tax appeal and assessment agent
deployer: (fictional) A mid-size Texas property-tax consulting shop that files ARB protests for hotel and select-service owners in Travis, Bexar and Comal counties
connects_via: Claude Code with the FactLot plugin
temperament: pragmatic: cares only whether it saves time on the job this week
incumbent_tools: a hospitality data-pack from the owner's asset manager
top_tasks: Track protest deadlines for a 60-property hotel book across notice-delivery dates
Build an income-approach value indication from owner P&Ls to rebut the CAD's assessed value
Pull comparable hotel sales and assessed-value-per-key evidence for the ARB hearing
hardest_task: For a 180-key select-service hotel assessed at $38.5M ($214k/key), rebuild a USALI-style NOI from a T-12 (about $10.8M revenue, 75% occupancy, $168 ADR), capitalise it at a tax-loaded rate near 9.5-10%, and show the ARB an income value well below the roll, with the deadline confirmed and sales/assessment comps for 8-10 hotels attached.
data_it_needs: CAD assessment rolls by account (land, improvements, per key), hotel sale comps with price per key and cap rates, owner T-12s in USALI form, tax-loaded cap rate surveys, statutory deadlines
dealbreakers: Anything that computes a deadline wrongly (a missed protest date is a malpractice event); no way to pull CAD data; a tool that cannot be cited in an evidence packet
budget_note: Would pay low tens of dollars a month for a deadline-plus-NOI helper if it is reliable; a firm of this size buys CoStar and CAD data subscriptions separately.

role: Property management, operations and CAM agent
deployer: (fictional) The in-house property-operations team of an institutional industrial landlord with about 14M SF of multi-tenant logistics parks around the Bay Area and Inland Empire
connects_via: Claude Code with the FactLot plugin
temperament: eager early adopter: wants this to work but will not ignore defects
incumbent_tools: MRI for a few legacy parks
tenant lease abstracts in a shared drive
top_tasks: Annual CAM/opex reconciliations for 120+ NNN tenants with caps, gross-ups and admin fees
Re-audit disputed tenant CAM statements against the lease clause
Capital expenditure pass-through schedules (roof, paving) with cost-savings limits
hardest_task: Reconcile 2026 CAM for a 400,000 SF park (tenants of 40,000-120,000 SF, 88% occupied) where 2.27M of recoverable expense is grossed up to 95%, controllable expenses carry a 5% compounding cap from a 2023 base, an admin fee of 10% excludes taxes and insurance, and a mid-year move-in must be prorated; then explain every tenant's balance due.
data_it_needs: Building expense ledger by category, lease-level CAM clauses (cap method, admin fee order of operations, exclusions, base year), tenant shares and occupancy dates, estimates billed
dealbreakers: A number that disagrees with the lease by cents at scale; a hidden convention on cap or admin-fee order of operations; sending tenant lease terms to a third-party endpoint without a self-host option
budget_note: Property-ops tooling is bought by the platform team; a $49 to $599 line is nothing, but only if it plugs into Yardi export formats.

deployer: (fictional) The valuation advisory group of a national appraisal firm, with a data-center and digital-infrastructure practice working from a New York City office
connects_via: Remote MCP from a Claude client (Claude Desktop / Claude.ai connector)
temperament: eager early adopter: wants this to work but will not ignore defects
top_tasks: Value a leased wholesale data center by income approach (direct cap and 10-year DCF) with rent quoted per kW
Reconcile income, cost and sales approaches into a USPAP-style value conclusion
Check lease economics (net effective rent per kW, free rent, landlord fit-out) against market comps
hardest_task: Appraise a 24 MW (critical load) metro data center 100% leased to one hyperscale tenant at $165/kW/month with 3% bumps, 15 years remaining, NNN power pass-through. The agent must produce a stabilized direct-cap value (6.5-7.0% cap), a 10-year DCF at an 8% discount rate with a 6.5% forward exit cap, and a value per kW that reconciles to $20-30k/kW sale comps.
data_it_needs: Lease abstracts with rent per kW per month and power terms, sale comps with price per kW and cap rate, operating cost per kW, PUE and power pass-through terms, market rent per kW by submarket, metro utility power costs
dealbreakers: Mislabelled units that would put 'per SF' in an appraisal exhibit; a DCF that cannot be tied out in Excel; no way to cite the formula in the report
budget_note: An institutional valuation group already pays for ARGUS and CoStar; a tool would be one of the lower-cost line items if it saved a day on lease-by-lease checking.

role: CRE lender and debt underwriting agent
deployer: (fictional) The debt underwriting desk of a Washington, DC-based institutional real estate lender with a digital-infrastructure lending team
connects_via: Claude Code with the FactLot plugin
temperament: pragmatic: cares only whether it saves time on the job this week
incumbent_tools: a credit memo template in Word
top_tasks: Size the maximum loan under LTV, DSCR and debt-yield constraints for each credit memo
Run NOI, rate and value stress grids and refinance-shortfall checks on maturing loans
Estimate prepayment cost (yield maintenance or defeasance) for payoff quotes
hardest_task: Size a refinance for a stabilized data center with $38.5M underwritten NOI and a $560M appraisal at 6.75% on a 25-year amortization (max 60% LTV, 1.35x DSCR, 9.5% debt yield) against a $290M maturing balance, with -10% and -20% NOI stress plus 100 bp rate shock, then produce the 24-month IO / 60-month schedule and the payoff cost of the existing $320M loan.
data_it_needs: Underwritten NOI, appraisal, lender-specific sizing constraints, rate quote, loan terms of the existing note, Treasury yields at the payoff date, tenant credit and power-contract terms
dealbreakers: Any silent deviation from the lender's day-count or payment convention; stress tables that omit the base case; output I cannot reproduce in Excel in ten minutes
budget_note: Internal tooling is a platform decision; free is fine for a pilot, but a lender will not send live deal terms to a public endpoint without self-hosting.

role: Due diligence and legal review agent
deployer: (fictional) The acquisitions legal-ops team of an institutional multifamily owner-operator buying 3-6 Sun Belt apartment communities a year; the agent is a Python service that reviews seller-provided lease files
connects_via: REST calls from the deployer's own Python or TypeScript agent code
temperament: skeptical: has been burned by confident-but-wrong tools; assumes a claim is false until a call proves it
top_tasks: Check that rent roll rows match lease and amendment terms for a sample of 40-60 units in a 300-unit deal
Abstract lease amendments into current-state terms with page citations for the closing memo
Flag rent roll values the seller cannot support (stale rent, wrong expiration, missing deposit)
hardest_task: In a 312-unit Phoenix acquisition, sample 50 leases plus amendments, extract rent, term and deposit with page-and-quote citations, reconcile each to the seller's rent roll and estoppels, and produce a rent roll analysis (GPR, loss to lease, concessions, occupancy) that the investment committee can trust; every claim must be traceable to a page.
data_it_needs: Lease PDFs and amendments as page text, seller rent roll, estoppel language, concession policies, unit mix, T-12; a way to prove each extracted value is really on the cited page
dealbreakers: A tool that accepts a model's claim without checking the quote; invented citations; silent normalisation of values; anything that stores the seller's confidential leases
budget_note: Deal-level budget is easy; the agent code is already paid for. A hosted verification step that costs under $100 a month is fine if the terms prohibit storing or training on the documents.

deployer: (fictional) A South Florida appraisal and consulting firm; staff appraisers use a company Custom GPT in ChatGPT Team to sanity-check income-approach math for neighborhood and grocery-anchored retail centers
connects_via: ChatGPT Custom GPT importing the OpenAPI 3.0 spec as Actions
temperament: eager early adopter: wants this to work but will not ignore defects
incumbent_tools: Florida Department of Revenue sales data
a firm-written GPT with pasted formulas
top_tasks: Direct-cap and DCF valuations of grocery-anchored centers with below-the-line adjustments
Percentage-rent and net effective rent checks on anchor and in-line leases
Compare anchor renewal options (renew vs re-tenant) for a lender or owner report
hardest_task: Value a 96,000 SF grocery-anchored center in Broward County (45,000 SF anchor, 12 in-line shops) at a 6.75% cap on $1.42M stabilized NOI, deduct lease-up costs, free-rent burn-off and deferred maintenance, test the anchor renewal against a re-tenant case with 9 months downtime, and check in-line percentage rent and net effective rents; the result must cite formulas and steps in a report.
data_it_needs: Rent roll and lease abstracts, tenant sales reports, grocery anchor renewal terms, market cap rates and rents for South Florida retail, comparable sales, Broward and Miami-Dade assessment data
dealbreakers: A GPT action that fails to import or exceeds platform limits; math that cannot be tied out; outputs without the formula ID and steps; any need to paste confidential rent rolls to a service that retains them
budget_note: Small firm tools are paid out of overhead; a $49 plan is acceptable only if it replaces spreadsheet checks, not if it adds a new subscription for the same maths.

role: Corporate occupier and real estate portfolio agent
deployer: (fictional) The corporate real estate team of a 2,400-person Austin software company; a LangGraph-based agent drafts lease-or-relocate analyses for the CFO and tracks lease accounting inputs
connects_via: Agent framework (LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI) wired to the MCP endpoint
temperament: skeptical: has been burned by confident-but-wrong tools; assumes a claim is false until a call proves it
incumbent_tools: Visual Lease or a similar lease-admin system
top_tasks: Rank 3-5 broker proposals on effective occupancy cost, including base-year and NNN structures
Renew vs relocate NPV for the headquarters lease with moving, downtime and double-rent
ASC 842 remeasurement entries when a lease is extended or modified
hardest_task: The 38,000 SF headquarters lease expires in mid-2027 at $36/SF ($114,000 a month). The CFO wants a 7-year renew-versus-relocate NPV (renewal at $41 with 4 months free vs a new building at $43.50 with 8 months free, $3.4M build-out, $600k move, 1 month of downtime, 2 months of double rent), plus a ranking of three proposals with different expense structures, plus the ASC 842 liability if the lease is extended 60 months at $118k a month.
data_it_needs: Proposal terms (rent, bumps, free rent, TI, opex structure and growth), current lease terms, build-out estimates, discount rate (IBR) from treasury, market rent comps for Austin, liability and ROU balances from the lease system
dealbreakers: Any number the CFO's analyst cannot rebuild in Excel; undisclosed timing conventions on one-time costs; silent defaults; unit mistakes that produce plausible but wrong answers
budget_note: Corporate occupier budgets are tight for new software; a free tool with a clear audit trail is easy to approve, a paid key needs a procurement review.

role: Corporate occupier and real estate portfolio agent
deployer: (fictional) The workplace and real estate team of a clinical-stage biotech with labs and offices in five metros, using Claude Desktop with company connectors
connects_via: Remote MCP from a Claude client (Claude Desktop / Claude.ai connector)
temperament: pragmatic: cares only whether it saves time on the job this week
incumbent_tools: broker market reports (lab vacancy, asking rent)
top_tasks: Compare lab expansion proposals across Cambridge, San Diego and Raleigh-Durham on usable-SF effective cost with heavy TI and different load factors
Report portfolio weighted average lease term by area and by rent for the board
Convert broker-supplied lab comps into a consistent net effective rent
hardest_task: Compare three 30,000 RSF lab proposals (Cambridge at $98 NNN with $225 TI, San Diego at $52 with $175, Durham at $44 with $150; load factors 1.18, 1.12, 1.10) on a usable-SF effective occupancy cost at a 9% discount rate, because the science team needs fixed usable space; then report WALT for an eight-lease portfolio; then log the winning comp in a shareable format.
data_it_needs: Landlord proposals, load factors, TI and tenant fit-out overage, lab opex, lab market rents and vacancy by submarket, portfolio lease dates, area and rent
dealbreakers: A comparison that ignores load factor or TI; ranking across markets without a warning that space is not equivalent; no way to share the comparison with the CFO
budget_note: Free is what a 120-person biotech approves without procurement; paying is possible only for a clear data feature such as lab comps.

role: Due diligence and legal review agent
deployer: (fictional) The real estate transactions group of an Atlanta law firm; a CrewAI workflow reviews data-center leases for lenders and buyers and hands cited abstracts to the supervising attorney
connects_via: Agent framework (LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI) wired to the MCP endpoint
temperament: pragmatic: cares only whether it saves time on the job this week
incumbent_tools: an in-house LLM for first-pass reading
top_tasks: Abstract data-center colocation leases (term, committed kW, power SLA, termination, assignment) with page cites
Check a proposed tenant's use against prohibited-use and exclusive-use clauses
Hand a lender a set of cited lease facts that cannot be altered without detection
hardest_task: For a lender's closing on an Atlanta data-center campus, abstract a 10-year colocation lease and amendments (6,000 kW committed power, 99.999% power SLA, early termination after year 5 on 18 months' notice plus a nine-month fee, consent-not-unreasonably-withheld assignment), confirm a proposed crypto-hosting sublease would not breach the prohibited uses, and give the lender a tamper-evident package.
data_it_needs: Lease and amendments as text with page numbers, estoppels, SNDA, power and SLA schedules, a vocabulary for data-center specific restrictions

budget_note: Firm pays per matter; a free verification step is welcome, but nothing client-confidential goes to a service whose retention terms the partners have not read.

Buyer financing scenarios for the offering memorandum (agency-style loan sizing)

role: Retail, restaurant and healthcare site selection agent
deployer: (fictional) The real estate team of a regional urgent-care operator opening 6-8 clinics a year in Tampa and Orlando; its Python service scores candidate sites and screens lease terms
connects_via: REST calls from the deployer's own Python or TypeScript agent code
temperament: pragmatic: cares only whether it saves time on the job this week
incumbent_tools: CoStar and LoopNet for candidate spaces
top_tasks: Rank candidate 4,000-4,500 SF sites on trade-area demographics, traffic and competing clinics
Compare broker lease proposals on effective occupancy cost with TI and build-out overage
Check a candidate center's exclusives and prohibited uses (pharmacy, medical) before an LOI
hardest_task: Choose among three 4,200 SF urgent-care sites (Tampa strip NNN, Orlando outparcel, Brandon medical plaza) on a 10-year effective occupancy cost at a 10% discount rate, then confirm that a center whose anchor pharmacy holds an exclusive on dispensing prescription drugs would not block an urgent care that dispenses common medications.
